subject.title: Dashboard /compact silently wipes context once Claude CLI session is over the 1M cap

question: For over-cap or manually compacted Claude CLI sessions, should OpenClaw clear or reseed the Claude CLI resume binding from the compacted OpenClaw transcript, fully defer to Claude Code and show that limitation in Dashboard, or fail loudly with export/reset guidance?
rationale: The current behavior crosses product semantics for backend-owned continuity, OpenClaw compaction checkpoints, and Dashboard recovery UX; source changes alone cannot decide which session-continuity contract existing users should get.

options.title: Own Recovery At Compaction Boundaries
options.body: After OpenClaw-managed manual compaction or detected over-cap failure, clear or reseed the Claude CLI binding so the next turn uses the compacted transcript, and fail loudly with export/reset guidance when that cannot be guaranteed.

options.title: Document Full Backend Deferral
options.body: Keep Claude CLI continuity entirely backend-owned, hide or disable Dashboard compaction for that path, and explain that users must use reset/export when Claude Code itself cannot compact.

options.title: Wait For Narrow Linked Work
options.body: Hold this issue behind #84593 and #93198 until maintainers can separate context-budget persistence from resume-binding invalidation and Dashboard UX.

recommendation.title: Own Recovery At Compaction Boundaries
recommendation.body: After OpenClaw-managed manual compaction or detected over-cap failure, clear or reseed the Claude CLI binding so the next turn uses the compacted transcript, and fail loudly with export/reset guidance when that cannot be guaranteed.

likelyOwner.reason: They landed the current native-compaction ownership behavior and are the best available routing point for deciding whether that contract should change at compaction boundaries.
